clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond arriving, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987 when you were fourteen: you clashed with your stepfather and distanced from him, you were drawn toward your father, your parents separated over having a baby, and you made the chess squad but felt out of your depth. These shifts in your relationships and your anxiety sit together in months when your stepmother's move prompted family change.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's death in June 1991 and the months after: your wrist injury stopped your playing and your anxiety rose, you fused with your roommate Rafe then fought with him and he moved out, you were getting high and absorbed in radios, you were low and unable to get going with your functioning falling, and your mother filled in your college forms while you underfunctioned. Your grandfather's death, your mother's remarriage that autumn, and the pile of shifts in your own life and friendships all fell within these months; the period settles as you found your footing again.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around 2001 when your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and in the months that followed: your anxiety was running high as you lost steam for performing and your functioning fell, you had a disastrous audition and were done with performing, you were on poor terms with family and friends and distanced from them, you left Thornbury, you met Marisol and moved to live with her then split from her within months, you sank into depression once you split and returned to Thornbury, you could not face your family and your anxiety rose, you relied on friends instead and turned toward them, and you stopped speaking to your mother when you moved away that summer. Your grandmother's illness, her final months in your parents' home, and the cascade of your own moves and relationship shifts all fell in these months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's death in January 2008 and the months after: you were too drained for conversation and distanced from your mother, she pressed to visit you at Alder Creek and your anxiety rose as you told her repeatedly the timing was wrong, you kept the door shut on her when she came, and you cut off contact with your mother when you moved to nursing school that summer. The period settles once you were at school and the silence held at a distance.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage in March 2017 and the months that followed into late 2019: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along and you moved away from her, your anxiety was constantly high as you felt you ought to drive your projects forward, you started a sleeping pill, your partner Wren was swamped one thing after another, you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, Wren talks all day with her father and brother and they are fused, you were awake from the small hours at a family weekend and could only pull back as others rose and felt you didn't belong, and Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. Your marriage, your partner's family structure, and the pile of shifts in both of your functioning and relationships all fell within these months as you navigated her family's closeness alongside your own distance from yours.

periods.name: the year you left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
